question.text: An investor holds listed equity shares for 14 months and sells them making a profit. What is the applicable capital gains tax treatment?

answer.text: Long-term capital gains tax applies as the holding period exceeds 12 months for listed equity shares
Short-term capital gains tax applies regardless of holding period
No capital gains tax as listed equity shares are exempt
Long-term capital gains applies only if held for more than 24 months

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, listed shares held for more than 12 months before sale produce long-term capital gains treatment. The investor held the listed equity for 14 months, which exceeds 12 months, so LTCG treatment applies. The Trap: Listed equity is not fully exempt and the 12-month threshold is not extended to 24 months. The 24-month period is not supported by the workbook pages cited for this question. Note: The workbook also gives the applicable LTCG/STCG rates for listed equity (with STT paid). The 12-month rule is the source-backed threshold; longer thresholds for other asset classes should be confirmed against the specific tax source before being applied.
